parts.latex: Which data collected about a virus could be classified as both categorical and nominal?

solutions.latex:
Categorical data is sorted into categories rather than measured or counted; nominal categories have no natural order.

The country where the virus originated is a name with no order, so it is categorical and nominal.

The number of people, the rate of spread and the length of time are all numerical, so they are not categorical (options A, C, D).

$$\therefore\ \text{the country the virus originated (option B)}$$

parts.latex: Which of the following is an example of discrete data?

solutions.latex:
Discrete data can only take particular separated values, usually found by counting.

The number of pets in a family is a count (0, 1, 2, ...), so it is discrete.

The species of fish is categorical, while tyre pressure and height are measured quantities that can take any value in a range (continuous).

Hence the correct option is B.

parts.latex:
Grace is collecting information for an orchardist who grows oranges.

She collects two oranges at random from each of 30 trees spread across the orchard and measures how much juice can be squeezed from each.

What type of variable is the data she collects?

solutions.latex:
The amount of juice is a measurement (for example, in mL), so it can take any value in an interval, not just counted values.

It is a number, not a category.

Hence it is a continuous numerical variable, which is option A.
